title.narrative: Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction

description.narrative: The development objective of Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction Project for Bangladesh is to reduce the vulnerability of people in targeted communities to riverine and flash floods and improve the country's capacity in disaster preparedness and response. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Resilient Flood Shelters and Community Infrastructure, has the following sub-components: (i) Resilient Flood Shelters; and (ii) Resilient Community Infrastructure. 2) The second component, Strengthening Capacity for Disaster Preparedness and Response and Technical Assistance, has the following sub-components: (i) Strengthening LGED's Capacity for Disaster Preparedness and Rehabilitation of Local Infrastructure; and (ii) Technical Assistance for Long-Term Community Flood Resilience. 3) The third component, : Project Management, Design and Supervision (D&S), Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E), aims support to project management, implementation, and M&E. 4) The fourth component, Contingency Emergency Response Component, aims to provide provision of immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed.
To reduce the vulnerability of people in targeted communities to riverine and flash floods and improve the country's capacity in disaster preparedness and response.

condition.narrative: (FA Section I.B of Schedule 2). For the purpose of implementing Part 3 of the Project, the PIU shall (i) appoint a D&S consultancyfirm to undertake the detailed design and bidding documents of the civil works, provide procurement support and supervise theconstruction of all the civil works and (ii) a M&E consultancy firm to provide support in monitoring Project progress andassociated impacts in the Project areas.

(FA Section III.C of Schedule 2). The Recipient shall ensure that in carrying out the activities/Subprojects under Part 1.2 of theProject the proceeds of the Financing are for expenditures towards such goods, works, consulting and non-consulting services,Operating Cost and Trainings that inter alia (i) are not otherwise financed; (ii) satisfies the Recipient's capacity and mandate tosupport the Subproject implementation and budget; (iii) is not an investment specified in the negative list ie. has negativeenvironmental impacts requires involuntary resettlement, finances private goods; and (iv) climate vulnerability profiles of thetargeted villages.

Expenditures to be Exclusively Financed with Counterpart Funds (FA Section I.D of Schedule 2). The Recipient shall ensure that thefollowing expenditures are financed exclusively out of its own resources and not out of the proceeds of the Credit: (i) all landrequired for the purposes of the Project, and provide, promptly as needed, the resources needed for this purpose; (ii) taxesexceeding 15%; (iii) recurrent expenditures such as workshop allowances, sitting allowances, cash per diems, honoraria and fuel;(iv) salaries of the Recipients civil servants; (v) purchase of vehicles; and (vi) maintenance expenditures of the multi-purposeshelters.

Institutional Arrangements (FA Section I.A of Schedule 2). The Recipient shall establish within three (3) months of the EffectiveDate and maintain, throughout the period of implementation of the Project, the Project Steering Committee ("PSC") with a mandate,composition and resources in accordance with the guidelines of the Ministry of Planning and satisfactory to the Association.

Institutional Arrangements (FA Section I.A of Schedule 2). Within three (3) months of the Effective Date, the Recipient shallestablish and maintain at all times during the implementation of the Project, a Project Implementation Committee (PIC), with amandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association.

Institutional Arrangements (FA Section I.A of Schedule 2). Within three (3) months of the Effective Date, the Recipient, shallestablish and maintain at all times during the implementation of the Project, the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) within theLGED, with functions and resources and staff in adequate numbers and with qualifications, experience and terms of referencesatisfactory to the Association.
